extracted.intended_audience: investment advisers (registered or required to be registered), broker-dealers, and compliance officers subject to the Investment Advisers Act of 1940
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards from the Investment Advisers Act governing identification of clients, transition rules, definitions of qualified clients, advertising/marketing (including testimonials, third-party ratings, and performance presentation), agency cross transactions, and custody requirements for client funds and securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of client for private investment companies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a private investment company, an investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, or a business development company, each equity owner of any such company (except for the investment adviser entering into the contract and any other equity owners not charged a fee on the basis of a share of capital gains or capital appreciation) will be considered a client for purposes of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity owners who are charged fees based on capital gains/appreciation are clients; the adviser itself and equity owners not charged such fees are excluded. This affects applicability of prohibitions and disclosure duties elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rule—registered advisers honoring old contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered investment adviser entered into a contract and satisfied the conditions of this section that were in effect when the contract was entered into, the adviser will be considered to satisfy the conditions of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if a natural person or company who was not a party to the original contract becomes a party (including an equity owner of a private investment company), the conditions in effect at the time that person becomes a party will apply to that person or company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rule—advisers previously not registered
rubrics_metrics.description: If an investment adviser was not required to register and was not registered at the time it entered into an advisory contract, section 205(a)(1) will not apply to that advisory contract or to accounts established when the adviser was not required to register and was not registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided, however, that section 205(a)(1) will apply with regard to a natural person or company who was not a party to the contract and becomes a party when the adviser is required to register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers by gift/bequest or divorce not causing new party status
rubrics_metrics.description: A transfer of an equity ownership interest in a private investment company by gift or bequest, or pursuant to an agreement related to legal separation or divorce, will not cause the transferee to 'become a party' to the contract for purposes of the transition rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This carve-out prevents routine familial transfers from triggering application of newer contract conditions under section 205(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified client—assets under management threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified client' includes a natural person or company that, immediately after entering into the contract, has under the management of the investment adviser at least the applicable dollar amount specified in the most recent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicable dollar amount is set by the Commission's most recent order (see 'most recent order' definition and inflation-adjustment rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified client—net worth or qualified purchaser test
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified client' includes a person whom the adviser reasonably believes, immediately prior to entering into the contract, either: (A) has a net worth (together with jointly held assets with spouse) exceeding the applicable dollar amount in the most recent order (with specific rules for calculating net worth); or (B) is a 'qualified purchaser' as defined in the Investment Company Act at the time the contract is entered into.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net worth calculation rules: do not include primary residence as an asset; indebtedness secured by primary residence up to fair market value is not included as a liability (except any increase in indebtedness in last 60 days beyond acquisition must be included); indebtedness secured by primary residence in excess of fair market value must be included as a liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified client—executive officers and employee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified client' includes (iii)(A) an executive officer, director, trustee, general partner, or person serving in a similar capacity of the investment adviser; or (iii)(B) an employee (other than purely clerical/administrative staff) who participates in the adviser's investment activities and has performed such functions for at least 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employee status requires substantive participation in investment activities and at least 12 months of such functions either for the adviser or in substantially similar roles at another company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions—company, private investment company, executive officer, most recent order
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule defines 'company' per section 202(a)(5) (excluding companies required to be registered under the Investment Company Act but not registered), 'private investment company' as a company that would be an investment company but for section 3(c)(1), 'executive officer' to include president, vice presidents in charge of principal business units, officers performing policy-making functions, and others with similar policy-making functions, and 'most recent order' as the most recently issued Commission order under paragraph (e) published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine scope of applicability for the qualified client and other provisions; consult the cited statutory sections for further nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation adjustments for dollar thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 205(e) of the Act, dollar amounts referenced in the qualified client tests are adjusted by Commission order approximately every five years using the Personal Consumption Expenditures Chain-Type Price Index (PCE): divide year-end PCE for the calendar year preceding the order by the year-end PCE for 1997; multiply $750,000 (for the assets-under-management threshold) or $1,500,000 (for the net worth threshold) by that quotient and round to the nearest $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders issued on or about May 1, 2026, and approximately every five years thereafter will set the adjusted amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for broker-dealers acting as investment advisers for certain communications
rubrics_metrics.description: An investment adviser that is a broker or dealer registered under section 15 of the Exchange Act is exempt from section 206(3) with respect to transactions in connection with which the broker-dealer is acting as an investment adviser solely by means of: (1) publicly distributed written materials or publicly made oral statements; (2) written/oral materials that do not purport to meet objectives or needs of specific individuals/accounts; (3) issuance of statistical information containing no expressions of opinion about investment merits; or (4) any combination of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such materials must include a statement that if the purchaser uses the adviser's services in connection with a sale/purchase of a security that is a subject of the communication, the adviser may act as principal or as agent for another person. This exemption is narrowly tied to the nature of the communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of publicly distributed written materials and oral statements (35-person threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the broker-dealer exemption, 'publicly distributed written materials' are those distributed to 35 or more persons who pay for such materials, and 'publicly made oral statements' are those made simultaneously to 35 or more persons who pay for access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric threshold determines whether the communication qualifies for the exemption; payments by recipients are relevant to the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cross transactions—client written consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An adviser (or related broker-dealer) is deemed in compliance with section 206(3) when effecting an agency cross transaction if the advisory client has executed a written consent prospectively authorizing such transactions, provided that the consent is obtained after full written disclosure that the adviser (or relying person) will act as broker for, receive commissions from, and have potentially conflicting loyalties and responsibilities regarding both parties to such transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must be prospective and follow full written disclosure clearly explaining the conflicts inherent in agency cross transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cross transactions—transaction confirmations requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each agency cross transaction, the adviser (or person relying on the rule) must send to each client a written confirmation at or before completion of the transaction containing: (i) a statement of the nature of the transaction; (ii) the date the transaction took place; (iii) an offer to furnish upon request the time when the transaction took place; and (iv) the source and amount of any other remuneration received or to be received by the adviser or any other person relying on the rule in connection with the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in a purchase neither adviser nor relying person participated in a distribution, or in a sale neither participated in a tender offer, the confirmation may state whether any other remuneration has been or will be received and that the source/amount will be furnished upon written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cross transactions—annual aggregated disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The adviser (or person relying on the rule) must send each such client, at least annually and with or as part of any written statement/summary of such account, a written disclosure identifying the total number of such transactions since the last statement and the total amount of all commissions or other remuneration received or to be received in connection with such transactions during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This annual statement provides aggregate transparency about frequency and compensation associated with agency cross transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cross transactions—consent revocability and prohibition on dual recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: All written disclosure statements and confirmations must include a conspicuous statement that the written consent may be revoked at any time by written notice; and no agency cross transaction may be effected in which the same adviser (or adviser and related person) recommended the transaction to both a seller and a purchaser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must be presented as revocable and advisers must avoid situations where they recommended the same transaction to both sides (prohibition against recommending to both buyer and seller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cross transactions—continued fiduciary duties
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule does not relieve the adviser or person relying on it from acting in the best interests of the advisory client, including the duty regarding best price and execution, nor from other disclosure obligations under section 206 or other federal securities laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with procedural disclosure/consent requirements is not a substitute for substantive best-interest obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing general prohibitions (advertisements may not...)
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not: (1) include any untrue statement of a material fact or omit a material fact necessary to avoid misleading; (2) include a material statement of fact the adviser has no reasonable basis to believe it can substantiate; (3) include information likely to cause a misleading implication/inference; (4) discuss potential benefits without fair and balanced treatment of material risks/limitations; (5) reference specific investment advice without fair and balanced presentation; (6) include or exclude performance results or present performance periods in a manner not fair and balanced; or (7) otherwise be materially misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are broad prohibitions that require both accuracy and fair balance in communications; omissions that produce misleading impressions are covered as well as affirmative misstatements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimonials and endorsements—required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not include any testimonial or endorsement, nor may an adviser provide compensation for one, unless the adviser ensures that at the time of dissemination: (i) clearly and prominently discloses whether the testimonial was given by a current client or the endorsement was given by a person other than a current client; (ii) discloses if cash/non-cash compensation was provided; and (iii) provides a brief statement of any material conflicts of interest of the person giving the testimonial/endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures must be clear and prominent; they are in addition to providing material terms of any compensation arrangement and descriptions of material conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimonials and endorsements—adviser oversight and written agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The investment adviser must have (i) a reasonable basis for believing the testimonial/endorsement complies with the rule's requirements; and (ii) a written agreement with any person giving a testimonial/endorsement that describes the scope of activities and terms of compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must exercise oversight and document arrangements—this is an affirmative compliance obligation, not merely reactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimonials and endorsements—disqualification and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An adviser may not compensate a person for a testimonial/endorsement if the adviser knows, or should know with reasonable care, that the person is an ineligible person (subject to a disqualifying Commission action or disqualifying event) at the time of dissemination; exemptions exist for de minimis compensation (≤ $1,000 in preceding 12 months), testimonials/endorsements by affiliates/employees (with disclosure of affiliation), certain broker-dealer recommendations subject to Reg BI, and persons covered by rule 506(d) of Regulation D in certain offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule contains nuanced exemptions and grandfathering for conduct before May 4, 2021; advisers must evaluate ineligibility and applicable exemptions carefully and document any reliance on exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party ratings—reasonable basis and disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not include any third-party rating unless the adviser: (1) has a reasonable basis for believing any questionnaire/survey used to prepare the rating is structured to make it equally easy to provide favorable and unfavorable responses and not designed to produce a predetermined result; and (2) clearly and prominently discloses (or reasonably believes the rating discloses): the date of the rating and period on which it is based; the identity of the third party that created/tabulated the rating; and, if applicable, that compensation was provided by the adviser in connection with obtaining or using the rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must vet third-party methodologies and provide transparent attribution and compensation disclosures to avoid misleading investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—gross vs. net presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: An adviser may not present gross performance in any advertisement unless the advertisement also presents net performance (i) with at least equal prominence and in a format facilitating comparison with gross performance, and (ii) calculated over the same time period, using the same type of return and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net performance must be presented no less prominently and with comparable calculation methodology to avoid misleading impressions created by gross figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—required time periods for portfolio/composite results
rubrics_metrics.description: Any performance results of any portfolio or composite aggregation (other than any private fund) must include performance results for one-, five-, and ten-year periods, each presented with equal prominence and ending on a date no less recent than the most recent calendar year-end; if the portfolio did not exist for a prescribed period, substitute the life of the portfolio for that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures multi-period perspective and comparability, with limited substitution when a portfolio's life is shorter than prescribed windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—prohibition on claiming Commission approval
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not state, expressly or impliedly, that the calculation or presentation of performance results has been approved or reviewed by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must avoid implying regulatory endorsement of their performance presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—related performance inclusion or permissible exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not present related performance unless it includes all related portfolios; however, related performance may exclude related portfolios if (i) advertised performance is not materially higher than if all related portfolios had been included, and (ii) the exclusion does not alter the presentation of any required time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions are permitted only where they do not materially inflate advertised returns or change required period presentations; advisers should document basis for any exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—extracted performance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An advertisement may not include any extracted performance unless it provides, or offers to provide promptly, the performance results of the total portfolio from which the performance was extracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advertising a subset's results, advisers must make the total portfolio results available to ensure context and prevent cherry-picking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—hypothetical performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Any hypothetical performance in an advertisement is prohibited unless the adviser: (i) adopts and implements policies/procedures reasonably designed to ensure the hypothetical performance is relevant to the likely financial situation and investment objectives of the intended audience; (ii) provides sufficient information to enable the audience to understand the criteria and assumptions used in calculating the hypothetical performance; and (iii) provides sufficient information to enable the audience to understand the risks and limitations of using such hypothetical performance for investment decisions (with special provision for private-fund investors to be provided or offered promptly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule distinguishes interactive analysis tools (which may be permitted if accompanied by methodological disclosures, explanation of variability, universe description/selectivity, and statement that results are hypothetical) from other hypothetical presentations; other conditions of the performance rules may be relaxed for hypothetical performance only as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance—predecessor performance conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Predecessor performance may not be used unless: (i) the person(s) primarily responsible for prior performance manage accounts at the advertising adviser; (ii) accounts managed at the predecessor adviser are sufficiently similar to the advertising adviser's accounts such that results are relevant; (iii) all accounts managed in a substantially similar manner are advertised unless exclusion would not materially increase performance and would not alter required time period presentation; and (iv) the advertisement clearly and prominently includes all relevant disclosures, including that the performance was from accounts managed at another entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of predecessor performance is tightly constrained to prevent misleading attribution of past results to current adviser capabilities; clear disclosure of origin and similarity is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement—definition and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisement means any direct or indirect communication an adviser makes to more than one person (or to one or more persons if the communication includes hypothetical performance) offering advisory services to prospective clients or investors in a private fund, or offering new advisory services to current clients; it excludes extemporaneous live oral communications, information in statutory/regulatory notices/filings reasonably designed to satisfy such requirements, and certain hypothetical-performance communications provided in response to unsolicited requests or in one-on-one communications with prospective/current private-fund investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition controls which communications are subject to the marketing rule; interactive and one-on-one communications and required regulatory filings are carved out in specific ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis compensation threshold for testimonials/endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'De minimis compensation' means compensation of $1,000 or less (or equivalent non-cash value) paid to a person for providing a testimonial or endorsement during the preceding 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonials/endorsements compensated at or below this threshold are exempt from certain requirements (e.g., some written-agreement provisions), but other disclosure obligations may still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualifying Commission action and disqualifying event definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'disqualifying Commission action' means a Commission opinion or order barring, suspending, or prohibiting a person from acting under the Federal securities laws. A 'disqualifying event' is any of several enumerated convictions, final orders, judgments, decrees, or Commission orders within ten years prior to dissemination that involve securities/fraud offenses or similar misconduct; certain orders/opinions may not be disqualifying if the person is in compliance and other conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine who is an 'ineligible person' for testimonial/endorsement compensation purposes, with detailed enumerated categories and limited exceptions (including compliance with prior orders and disclosure obligations for ten years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net performance definition and acceptable fee treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Net performance means performance after deduction of all fees and expenses a client/investor has paid or would have paid in connection with the adviser's services, including advisory fees, underlying vehicle advisory fees, and payments by the adviser for which the client reimburses the adviser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net performance may reflect exclusion of custodian fees paid to banks/third parties; if using a model fee, it must reflect either a deduction that would not produce higher performance than actual fees or a model fee equal to the highest fee charged to the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions—portfolio, related performance, related portfolio, predecessor performance, private fund, supervised person, testimonial, endorsement, extracted/gross/hypothetical performance, third-party rating, ineligible person
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule provides precise definitions for numerous terms: 'portfolio' (group of investments managed by the adviser), 'related performance' (performance of related portfolios/composites), 'related portfolio' (substantially similar investment policies/objectives/strategies), 'predecessor performance', 'private fund', 'supervised person', 'testimonial', 'endorsement', 'extracted performance', 'gross performance', 'hypothetical performance' (with inclusions/exclusions), 'third-party rating', and 'ineligible person'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine scope and trigger many of the marketing rule's obligations and prohibitions (see specific defined-term entries elsewhere). Interactive analysis tool treatment and examples are provided for hypothetical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody—qualified custodian safekeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An adviser has custody of client funds or securities only if a qualified custodian maintains those funds and securities either (i) in a separate account for each client under that client's name, or (ii) in accounts that contain only the adviser's clients' funds and securities under the adviser's name as agent or trustee for the clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of qualified custodians and proper account titling/segregation is required to avoid custody rule violations; custodial arrangements must meet these account-structure tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody—notice to clients when adviser opens account with qualified custodian
rubrics_metrics.description: If the adviser opens an account with a qualified custodian on a client's behalf (either under the client's name or under the adviser's name as agent), the adviser must notify the client in writing of the qualified custodian's name, address, and the manner in which the funds/securities are maintained promptly when the account is opened and following any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the adviser sends account statements to a client, include in the notification and subsequent statements a statement urging the client to compare the custodian's statements with those from the adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody—account statement requirement from qualified custodian
rubrics_metrics.description: The adviser must have a reasonable basis, after due inquiry, for believing that the qualified custodian sends an account statement at least quarterly to each client for which it maintains funds or securities, identifying amounts and all transactions during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must verify that custodians provide periodic independent account statements; encouraging client reconciliation helps detect discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody—independent verification (annual surprise examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Client funds and securities of which the adviser has custody must be verified by actual examination at least once each calendar year (except as otherwise provided) by an independent public accountant pursuant to a written agreement, at a time chosen by the accountant without prior notice and irregular from year to year. The agreement must provide for the first examination within six months of becoming subject to this paragraph, except if the adviser maintains client funds/securities as a qualified custodian, then the first examination must occur no later than six months after obtaining the internal control report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'surprise' independent examination requirement is a key control to detect custody misappropriation; written engagement terms and timing are prescribed and must be followed.
